### ① Derived judgments

Setup: `git rev-parse refs/review/pr-10479` = `600c330fc144bdf9eccbf5bd4ab4dfdc3e3b36ca` (unchanged). Merge-base `ab50ccc1`; 3 commits (`7ce2686`, `c49a2dc`, `600c330`); 3 files, +270/-69. `git diff --stat MB..head -- packages/core/` is empty, so core's resolver is read at head as-is.

1. Core ladder (`packages/core/src/utils/record-title.ts:534-617`): step 0 `recordDisplayValueAt(record, options.titleField)`; 1+2 `declaredNameField` = `nameField ?? displayNameField ?? NAME_FIELD_KEY`; 3 `formatTitleTemplate(objectDef.titleFormat)`; 4 `deriveTitleField`; 4b name-ish record keys; 5 `Record #id` / `Untitled` floor. So the ladder is displayField, nameField (plus aliases), titleFormat, derivation — as claimed. The `titleField` rung is fed `declaredDisplayField = fieldMeta?.displayField || fieldMeta?.reference_field || undefined` (`LookupField.tsx:314-315`), the same two keys `LookupCellRenderer` reads (`packages/fields/src/index.tsx:2396-2399`) and passes as `titleField` (`index.tsx:180`). It is a value rung: a declared pointer blank on the row falls through to nameField, where base returned an empty label (`'' ?? x` keeps `''`). Judged: exactly the field's own declaration under either spelling.

2. Renderers: old `formatRecordTitle` and core `formatTitleTemplate` share the placeholder regex `/\{([^{}]+)\}/g`, the separator class `[-–—|/·,:]`, the empty test (null, undefined, ''), and the strip/collapse/trim pass; both run on `shown`. Three widenings only: dotted paths walk nested objects, an object value reduces to its display name (old gave `[object Object]`), and `{{x}}` normalizes to `{x}` (old left the outer braces; base pin got `{Globex} / {HT-001}`). Old returned null on no-resolution, new returns '' and core skips falsy — same fall-through. Spec 17.4.0 `package/src/data/object.zod.ts:2122` reads verbatim "Placeholders may be written `{`{field}`}` or `{field}` — the title renderers treat the two as equivalent, normalizing `{`{field}`}` to `{field}` before substituting". So the double-brace change is spec-ruled and falls out of triage point 2 (reuse, do not copy); disclosed in the changeset. Not unruled. Side note, pre-existing and outside this PR: `PageHeaderRenderer` (`containers.tsx:351`) still interpolates single-brace only, while `DetailView` uses core's renderer (`DetailView.tsx:117`).

3. `name` default. Base chain `templated ?? shown[displayField defaulting to 'name'] ?? unified ?? tail`; head `unified(titleField: declared) ?? shown[declared ?? 'name'] ?? tail`. The cycle argument holds: once the template drops below nameField, "template above the name guess" and "name guess above nameField" cannot both survive; keeping the guess above the resolver (ablation A1) makes a template-only object with `name` rows show `name`, contradicting triage pin 3 and base. Spec `field.zod.ts:1370`: displayField "defaults to the referenced object's name/title" — the object's own resolution, which the cell renderer already applies. Inside the card. No-schema path: `unified` stays undefined, so label = `shown[declared ?? 'name'] ?? shown.label ?? shown.name ...`, byte-equivalent to base (checked against `LookupField.base.tsx:170-190`). Labels move for undeclared lookups when a schema is present in two cases: (a) nameField or alias is not `name` and rows carry `name` — disclosed; (b) UNDISCLOSED: the object declares neither key, rows carry `name`, but derivation picks another field because `name` is absent from `objectDef.fields` or typed in `NON_TITLE_TYPES` (for example `auto_number`) — base showed `name`, head shows the derived field (`toPredicateRecord`, `predicate-record.ts:123-160`, only collapses expanded relations, so the row's `name` survives on every path). This matches the cell renderer, whose docblock (`index.tsx:165-172`) excludes autonumber on purpose, and is what the resolver reuse implies; the changeset's "Upgrade effect" names only (a). Not a blocker.

4. Guard. `ba0b61a`: `DetailView.resolveDisplayTitle` = primaryField, declared pointer (1b), titleFormat, unified, schema.title, record keys, floor; `PageHeaderRenderer` = explicit schema.title, declared pointer, template, unified, record keys, placeholder. This PR = field's declared displayField, declared pointer, template, derivation, record keys, widget tail. All three rank an explicit per-view or per-field pointer above the declared pointer and the declared pointer above the template; displayField's position agrees with triage 5820783707. Guard not tripped; no return to card owed.

5. Call sites: `grep -c 'recordToOption(' LookupField.head.tsx` = 10 = 1 definition + 9 calls (head lines 692, 781, 788, 813, 905, 1000, 1081, 1157, 1174). All 9 pass `declaredDisplayField` and `refObjectSchema`; none passes a template. `refTitleFormat` at head: 2 hits (its `useMemo` at 476 and `titleFormat={refTitleFormat}` to `RecordPickerDialog` at 1677) against 15 on base; no option-label path reads it. Dep arrays for `fetchedOptions`, `resolveSelectedOption`, `recentOptions` and the quick-create callback (which lists both `displayField` for the create payload at 1173 and `declaredDisplayField` for the label) are complete for what each body reads. `handlePickerSelectRecords` now lists `refObjectSchema`, which its body passes to `recordToOption`; base listed `refTitleFormat` instead, so the closure refreshed only when the template string changed — the addition is right and closes a latent stale-schema closure. The hydration effect keeps its eslint-disabled deps excluding `refObjectSchema`, `perms`, `dataSource` — pre-existing, unchanged in kind; the `displayField` to `declaredDisplayField` swap triggers identically.

6. FLS: `shown = withoutDeniedFields(record, readable)` (`head:204-213`, drops denied keys). The resolver call, its `titleField` rung, template, derivation (read at the derived name on `shown`), record-key probe and the widget tail all read `shown`; only `val` and the floor test read `record.id`. All 9 calls pass a gate (`readable` or `fieldReadGate(perms, referenceTo, idField)`). `description` reads `record[descriptionField]` at base:179 and head:170 alike — pre-existing and pinned by 10373 as intended. Gate holds on every path.

7. Out-of-scope findings. (i) `lookupColumnDisplay.tsx:190-208` still renders `titleFormat` first for the display column through a private single-brace renderer; on an object declaring both keys the dropdown now reads nameField while the picker column reads the template — a disagreement this PR creates (both read the template before). It is the same ruling's next branch and outside the claimed file surface; PR body and changeset both name it. Correctly left out; must be carded. (ii) Hydration: the effect (`head:748-843`) captures `refObjectSchema` null on mount, its deps exclude it, and `findOption` (`head:846-855`) resolves an already-hydrated id from `pickerResolvedRecords`, so the schema's arrival never relabels. A bare-id value on an object whose nameField is not `name` shows the chip `name` while dropdown, cell and record page show the nameField value; on base both dropdown and chip showed `name`. Not a regression of the chip, and fewer surfaces disagree than on base, but it is the common edit-form state. Correctly left out; should be carded promptly.

Pins: `LookupField.labelOrder-10343.test.tsx` has 6 `it(` cases covering triage's three pins plus blank-pointer, double-brace and chip controls; every fixture row carries `name`, so a name-first order cannot pass. Repo-wide `formatRecordTitle` live references in `packages/fields` at head: 0 (the 11 grep hits are CHANGELOGs, comments and app-shell's existing alias export).

### ② Semver level

`'@object-ui/fields': patch`. AGENTS.md "版本号策略" (lines 267-273) rules only that major follows `@objectstack`, `major` is never declared (CI-enforced), and objectui's own breaking changes are `minor`; no rule fixes patch versus minor for a visible bug-fix behaviour change. `.changeset/config.json` places `@object-ui/fields` in the 39-package `fixed` group; on `refs/review/main` 1984 changesets are pending, 641 declaring `minor` (the three `9436-*` files among them, all `minor`), so the group bumps minor regardless of this file. The 9436 siblings graded the same ruling `minor`; this branch chose `patch` — inconsistent, not rule-breaking. The PR body's "as dispatched" is unsupported: claim comment 5825931515 names the changeset file, not a level. `Changeset Bump Policy` check: success.

Prose, sentence by sentence: the Before and After bullets are true against the base and head chains; "the same call the lookup cell renderer already makes" is true (`index.tsx:180`); "still reads `name` for quick-create and the picker's display column" is true (`head:1173`, `head:1676`); "Without the object's schema the label reads `name` first, as before" is true; the `{`{field}`}` sentence is true against `object.zod.ts:2122` and the base pin result; "The browse-all record picker's display column ... still shows the template" is true (`lookupColumnDisplay.tsx:190`). "Upgrade effect" is true but incomplete: it omits case (b) in ①.3.
